'''Port Phasmatys''' ({{IPAc-en|jagex|f|æ|z|ˈ|m|æ|t|ɪ|s}} {{respell|faz|MAT|iss}}) is a small town located on the north-eastern coast of [[Morytania]]. Once a coastal hub, the town was decimated by [[vampyres]] and is now populated by ghosts, making a [[ghostspeak amulet]] or [[Morytania legs 2]] necessary to talk to the majority of the inhabitants.

Entry to the town through the [[Energy Barrier (Port Phasmatys)|energy barriers]] requires two [[ecto-token]]s unless [[Ghosts Ahoy]] has been completed. Alternatively, a [[charter ship]] can be used to bypass the ecto-token requirement.

== Transportation ==
Several transport options bring players into or close to Port Phasmatys, listed here with their arrival destination. From closest to farthest:

* {{plink|Ectophial}} — [[Ectofuntus]], just north of town.
* {{plink|Charter ships|pic=War ship}} — eastern docks.
* {{plink|Fairy ring|pic=Fairy ring (Construction) icon}} {{Fairycode|alq}} — [[Haunted Woods]], west of the town.
* {{plink|Drakan's medallion}} — [[Ver Sinhaza]], a short run south of [[Andras]]' boat.
* {{plink|Fenkenstrain's Castle Teleport|txt=Fenkenstrain teleport}} — [[Fenkenstrain's Castle]] entrance, far west of the town.
* {{plink|Salve Graveyard Teleport|txt=Salve Graveyard teleport}} — [[Salve Graveyard]], very far west of the town.

==History==
Port Phasmatys dates back to the late [[Fourth Age]] and was founded by [[human]] settlers who had travelled to [[Morytania]], which at that time was not considered more dangerous than other places around Gielinor.{{CiteText|text=Display case (Varrock Museum, number 15)|quote=4th Age - yr 1777 Temple records show that human settlers came to the temple on the River Salve looking for new lands in which to settle. While there were legends that the temple on the Salve was blocking great evil, they refused to heed the warnings of the then custodians of the temple, thinking them possibly behind the times or reciting old legends. The lands of Misthalin and Asgarnia weren't the safest places in the world - the human tribes of these times were having constant troubles with goblins, hobgoblins, giants, etc., so how much worse could Morytania have been? So, human settlers passed over the Salve into Morytania. The Museum recently came into possession of this torn map showing the expansion routes of the settlers.}}{{CiteNPC|npc=Reldo|loc=Dragon Slayer II|quote=According to this there was a family by the name of Corvo living in Avarrocka for most of the Fourth Age. The last entry is from the year 1770 of the Fourth Age. [Player: What happened to them?] Impossible to say for sure but it was around that time that many people left Misthalin to settle in Morytania. (…) Port Phasmatys is where most of the Morytania settlers wound up.}} It was once a thriving port that frequently traded with those who came from the [[Wushanko Isles|Eastern Lands]] until [[Lowerniel Drakan|Lord Lowerniel Drakan]], the ruler of Morytania, took notice of the humans settling in his kingdom and demanded that they paid blood tithes to the [[vampyre]]s; the people of Port Phasmatys had no choice but to give in to his demands.{{CiteNPC|npc=Velorina|quote=It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas. We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us. He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.|loc=Ghosts Ahoy|notes=|name=}}

Over time, their numbers dwindled, and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands when [[Necrovarus]], a powerful mage from the [[Eastern Lands]], arrived.{{CiteNPC|npc=Velorina|quote=He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.|loc=Ghosts Ahoy|notes=|name=}} Claiming he had a vision of a great power beneath the town, a pool of ectoplasm was discovered deep below Phasmatys, and Necrovarus showed the citizens how to build the [[Ectofuntus]]. The Ectofuntus indeed repelled the vampyres, but it brought other issues. The people of the town began to lose any desire for food and water until their bodies shrivelled and died, and when a citizen died, they were unable to move on to the afterlife due to the psychic barrier created by Necrovarus, causing their ghosts to remain stuck in Port Phasmatys. This fate was Necrovarus' intention all along; eventually, there were no living inhabitants left, and the town fell into disrepair.{{CiteNPC|npc=Velorina|loc=Ghosts Ahoy|quote=Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres. (…) Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another – Ectopower. Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.}}

The vampyres gave up trying to collect blood tithes as there was no longer any blood to harvest, and the Ectofuntus continued to repel vampyres regardless.{{CiteNPC|npc=Velorina|quote=Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working.|loc=Ghosts Ahoy|notes=|name=}} By this time, the town was mostly abandoned, but sailors, traders and pirates did occasionally visit. Any visitors to the town are required to worship the Ectofuntus as so to maintain the Ectopower that lets its residents stick around as ghosts. Eventually, [[Ghosts Ahoy#Using the spell|an adventurer came along and freed the inhabitants]] from Necrovarus' control, allowing them to freely choose to pass on if they wished.
[[File:Phasmatys docks.png|thumb|The ghostly docks of Phasmatys.]]

==Locations==
===Ectofuntus===
{{Main|Ectofuntus}}[[File:Ectofuntus temple.png|thumb|The temple for the Ectofuntus.]]
After starting the [[Ghosts Ahoy]] [[quest]], you can worship the [[Ectofuntus]] to receive 4 times [[Prayer]] [[experience]] for every bone. Completing the quest will help immensely, as you can use the [[Ectophial]] to teleport back and forth, as well as bank at the town for free if needed. Players who have completed various levels of the [[Morytania Diary]] will be able to claim [[Bucket of slime|slime]] and [[Bonemeal (bones)|bonemeal]] daily from [[Robin|Robin Hood]] in exchange for bones, as well as receive the ability to teleport to the slime pit several times a day.

Many players use [[amulets of glory]] or [[rings of dueling]] to teleport to a [[Port Phasmatys bank|bank]], as it is faster than running to the bank in Port Phasmatys. A [[ghostspeak amulet]] will still be needed to talk to the disciples.

=== Docks ===
The town docks connect to multiple ports across [[Gielinor]]. [[Ak-Haranu]], a merchant from the [[Eastern Lands]] who runs [[Ak-Haranu's Exotic Shop.|Ak-Haranu's Exotic Shop]], can also be found on the docks. He can sell players [[bolt rack]]s to be used as ammunition for [[Karil's crossbow]].

The northern docks, found just north of the town, contain [[Andras]] and [[Pirate Pete]].

===Charter ship===
{{Charter ship fares}}
After completing [[Cabin Fever]], the charter ship fare is reduced by 50%. Wearing the [[Ring of Charos(a)]] also reduces the fare by 50%. These two bonuses can be stacked to reduce the cost to 25%.

=== Buildings ===
[[File:Port Phasmatys General Store.png|thumb|The crumbling general store of Port Phasmatys.]]
Many of the ghosts require payment in [[ecto-token]]s, which is the currency of the town, though the shop still uses [[coins]]. See the [[#Ectofuntus|Ectofuntus guide]] above or the [[Ghosts Ahoy]] [[quest]] for a guide to obtaining ecto-tokens.

After the player dismisses the message, they can use the bank.

=== Other ===
South of the town is the [[Morytania Spider Cave|Morytania spider cave]], a creepy cave containing the spider boss [[Araxxor/Strategies|Araxxor]]. North of the town is the shipwreck, an old, derelict ship containing the [[old crone]]'s [[Old man|lost son]]. There are also several [[yew trees]] in the area. There are no item spawns in this area.

==Inhabitants==

=== Personalities ===

* {{Chatl|Alice}}, a farmer who runs [[Alice's farm|her farm]] with her dearly departed husband, [[Malcolm]].
* {{Chatl|Ak-Haranu}}, a traveller from the [[Wushanko Isles]].
* {{Chatl|Andras}}, an emaciated resident of [[Slepe]] who ferries players there for a high fee.
* {{Chatl|Bill Teach}}, an adventurous pirate with many, many enemies.
* {{chatl|Cow31337Killer}}, a high-level player who kills <s>cows</s> chickens.
* {{Chatl|Droalak}}, a man who left for a far-off outpost against the wishes of his wife — and died!
* Three {{Chatl|Ghost banker|txt=ghost bankers}}, who ghostily help you access the [[Bank of Gielinor]].
* {{Chatl|Ghost captain (ghostship)|pic=Ghost captain chathead|txt=Ghost captain (ship)}}, a ghost captain who will take players nowhere since his ship won't work.
* {{Chatl|Ghost captain|txt=Ghost captain (rowboat)}}, a ghost captain who will take players to [[Dragontooth Island]].
* Three {{Chatl|Ghost disciple|txt=ghost disciples}}, followers of the evil [[Necrovarus]].
* Two {{Chatl|Ghost guard|txt=ghost guards}}, who charge [[ecto-tokens]] for town entrance.
* {{Chatl|Ghost innkeeper}}, an innkeeper that no longer sells beverages.
* Eight{{Chatl|Ghost sailor|txt=ghost sailors}}, sailors who are now bound to the port by its horrible curse.
* {{Chatl|Ghost shopkeeper}}, the owner of the general store.
* {{Chatl|Ghost villager|txt=Ghost villagers}}, villagers who live (or perhaps, unlive) throughout the town.
* {{Chatl|Goopy snake|pic=Goopy snake}}, a harmless and adorable snake, which swims underneath the [[Ectofuntus]].
* {{Chatl|Gravingas}}, an anti-Necrovarus activist.
* {{Chatl|Lyra}}, a non-ghostly gardener and the daughter of Alice and Malcolm.
* {{chatl|Malcolm}}, the dearly departed husband of [[Alice]].
* {{Chatl|Melina}}, the dearly departed wife of [[Droalak]].
* {{Chatl|Metarialus}}, a brewer found in the inn's basement.
* {{Chatl|Necrovarus}}, the leader of an ancient cult who has trapped the town's residents as ghosts.
* {{Chatl|Old man}}, the son of the [[old crone]], who was lost for a great deal of time.
* {{chatl|Robin}}, a famous archer and one of the few humans in the town.
* {{Chatl|Sarah (Port Phasmatys)|txt=Sarah}}, the descendant of a great warrior.
* {{chatl|Sneaky undead fowl}}, a cunning chicken-like creature that evades all attempts at capture.
* {{Chatl|Tool Leprechaun|txt=Tool leprechaun}}, a green-clad fellow who can store gardening supplies and note produce.
* {{Chatl|Trader Crewmember|pic=Trader Crewmember (1) chathead|txt=Trader crewmembers}}, ostentatiously-clad crewmembers who ferry players for exorbitant prices.
* {{Chatl|Velorina}}, a ghost who starts the [[Ghosts Ahoy]] quest and gives spare [[Ectophial|ectophials]].

=== Monsters ===

* [[Rat]] (x2)
* [[Swamp Crab|Swamp crabs]] (x5)
* [[Tortured soul]] (x8)
* [[Undead chicken]] (x6)
* [[Undead cow]] (x4)
[[Bats]] and aggressive [[leeches]] and [[vampyres]] can also make their way into the area from the nearby Haunted Woods.

==Trivia==
*"Phásma" ("[[wiktionary:φάσμα|φάσμα]]") is Ancient Greek for apparition or phantom, referencing the town being inhabited by ghosts.
